children: Chevron is taking steps to more than double its production in Venezuela, planning to invest more than $7 billion in the country over the next five years. The company says Wednesday it has entered multiple agreements with the country, establishing updated terms with its joint ventures to support future investment, project development and production growth. The agreements came after President Trump last week said the U.S. reached a deal with Venezuela to secure control of a big chunk of the country's oil reserves. "With improved terms and additional acreage, we are strengthening a portfolio that we believe can deliver attractive low-cost oil growth, support energy supply and create differentiated long-term value," Chevron CEO Mike Wirth says. (connor.hart@wsj.com)
